basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 8.' and it opens '(Vers. 8.) Et mortuus est Abraham in senectute bona, senex et plenus, et collectus est ad'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 8.) Et mortuus est Abraham in senectute bona, senex et plenus, et collectus est ad populum suum. Male in Septuaginta Interpretibus additum est, et deficiens Abraham mortuus est: quia non convenit Abrahae deficere, et imminui. Illud quoque quod nos posuimus, in senectute bona senex et plenus: in Graecis codicibus ponitur, plenus dierum. Quod cum sensum videatur exponere, eo quod luce et diei operibus plenus occubuerit: tamen magis ad anagogen facit, si simpliciter ponatur plenus.
